title: Cherokee War of 1776
summary: In 1776 Cherokee warriors, including followers of Dragging Canoe, attacked frontier settlements. South Carolina, North Carolina and Virginia forces answered by burning Cherokee towns in the Lower, Valley and Overhill areas; sources count 36 to 52 towns and crops destroyed. Older leaders Little Carpenter and Oconostota accepted neutrality and land cessions, while Dragging Canoe led followers to Chickamauga Creek.

uncertainty.note: Start is the 20 July 1776 clash near the Holston River (American Indian magazine); armies marched from late July to mid-October, so the end is given to the year only.

where.modern_name: Chota, Monroe County, Tennessee, USA (Overhill Cherokee towns; campaign also covered western North Carolina and upper South Carolina)
where.historical_name: Cherokee homeland: Overhill, Middle, Valley and Lower Towns, on the colonial frontier of Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina

importance.justification: Broke Cherokee power in the southern Appalachians, cost land, and split the nation between accommodation and the Chickamauga resistance.

audience_note: Describes the burning of dozens of Cherokee towns and food stores, which displaced many people, some of whom fled to Florida.
